lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: List Voltline Robotics before Clearwater Sensors.
items.because: Experience is usually listed newest first, and Voltline is the most recent role.

items.says: Use one consistent date style throughout.
items.because: Uniform formatting would look more polished.

items.says: Include relevant work, projects, or other experience from the gap after graduation if there is any.
items.because: There is a gap before the first listed role.

items.says: Check bullet indentation, spacing, date alignment, and line wraps in the final PDF.
items.because: Several entries wrap across lines in the supplied text.

items.says: Make the code portfolio address a complete, clickable URL.
Link directly to relevant portfolio work if it is available.
Consider adding a relevant concentration, honors, or coursework.
items.because: It may strengthen the résumé's fit for targeted jobs.

items.says: Make the test-time unit unambiguous and clarify what production scale the monthly volume describes.
Clarify what the percentages measure and the period or batch compared.
items.because: That would make the reduction easier to assess.

items.says: Define “calibration drift complaints” and the comparison period.
items.because: The measure is not fully defined.

items.says: Clarify that both throughput figures use the same measurement basis and station or process.
Define “update speed” and identify its comparison baseline.
items.because: Otherwise, the 60% improvement is hard to interpret.

items.says: Add a result such as test duration, coverage, or a defect caught if available.
items.because: The test count shows scale but not the rig's impact.

items.says: Distinguish the logger's data capture from the subsequent root-cause analysis.
Clarify whether the five failures were separate incidents or failure types.
Sampling a 5 kHz component at 8 kHz does not generally capture it without aliasing.
items.because: The rate does not meet the usual Nyquist condition; any filtering or other technique that made the claim valid is not explained.

items.says: Declaring the shared counter volatile does not by itself fix a race condition.
items.because: Volatile alone does not make shared access safe without proper synchronization or atomicity.

items.says: Consider placing the motor-controller accomplishment first under Voltline.
items.because: It is the strongest quantified embedded-systems accomplishment.

items.says: Clarify what the firmware rewrite covered.
Give the period or basis for the field-fault reduction if available.
Be prepared to explain whether the overlapping weather-station project was personal work outside Voltline.
items.because: Its dates overlap with the Voltline role.

items.says: Replace the “next-generation” bullet with concrete technical work or a verifiable outcome.
items.because: The promotional language does not tell a hiring manager what was built.

items.says: Add measurement conditions or operating assumptions if they materially affect the current comparison.
Make the public schematics and firmware easy to find through the portfolio link.
Clarify the role in the school's builds if it went beyond publishing the materials.
Resolve the mismatch between the student race-car title and leadership role and the robot-fleet bullets.
items.because: The title and role suggest a race-car project, but the bullets refer to a robot fleet.

items.says: Specify the firmware and testing work personally owned.
items.because: “Worked on” is vague and does not show the contribution.

items.says: Remove this bullet if later bullets cover the same work.
Use active wording and clarify what was personally implemented or tested.
items.because: The passive construction obscures the role.

items.says: Explain what the dashboard testing verified.
Check that the dashboard work is relevant to targeted positions.
The robot-fleet motor-controller accomplishment closely duplicates the Voltline accomplishment.
items.because: The fleet scale and performance results could be mistaken for copied or double-counted work rather than distinct project work.

items.says: C and C++ are languages and STM32 is a platform, not tools.
items.because: The skills are classified under the wrong type.

items.says: Organize skills by type.
items.because: That helps hiring teams and screening systems identify languages, platforms, and equipment.

items.says: Replace the broad “firmware” skill with specific, substantiated methods or technical areas.
items.because: “Firmware” is broad.

items.says: CAN is a protocol rather than a method.
items.because: It is classified under the wrong type.

items.says: Add relevant tools or platforms actually used.
